summary: Iteration 5 review PASSED. Backend: 10/10 pytest cases in test_iteration5_google.py pass — POST /api/auth/session with bogus session_id returns 401 with a Spanish detail ('Sesión de Google no válida o expirada'), missing body → 422, wrong field name (session_token) → 422; existing email/password regression is intact (ana.demo login 200 with access+refresh+user; /auth/me 200; /auth/refresh rotates and old refresh 401; register throwaway user 201; wrong password → generic 401 without the 'Google' message). Backend startup log is clean (Sentinel API ready, no errors); GET /api/ returns 200. Frontend (web preview, 390x844): (a) /onboarding/account renders google-signin-button labelled 'Continuar con Google' in register mode and 'Entrar con Google' after tapping 'Ya tengo cuenta'. (b) Clicking the button performs a full-page redirect first to https://auth.emergentagent.com/oauth/?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsentinel-audit-6.preview.emergentagent.com%2F (redirect param matches app origin + '/') and then onward to accounts.google.com — no real Google login attempted. (c) Return-path robustness: opening /#session_id=bogus-session with no stored session yields exactly ONE POST /api/auth/session → 401, no exchange loop, no red screen; app falls back to onboarding/terms (final URL is /onboarding/terms after the local-onboarding redirect from index.tsx). (d) Return-path with existing session: after logging in as ana.demo (ends on /map), opening /?session_id=bogus2 fires ONE /auth/session 401 then falls back to /auth/me 200, the user stays logged in and the Azure Maps static image renders on /map — no red screen. (e) Regression: /drive?lat=40.4168&lng=-3.7038&place=Sol&fromLat=40.45&fromLng=-3.69 still renders with drive-instruction 'Gire a la derecha en Calle de Santiago Bernabéu', drive-eta 'en 110 m · 22 min · 7.5 km · llegada 19:35', map-static-image with route. Console still shows the known-ignorable shadow*/pointerEvents RN Web deprecation warnings.

minor.issue: Soft-deleted-user resurrection edge case: /auth/session first queries {email, deleted_at: None}. If no live user is found it inserts a fresh doc; if the email is already stored on a soft-deleted user, insert throws DuplicateKeyError and the fallback `find_one({email})` (no deleted_at filter) returns the soft-deleted user and tokens are issued for it, effectively un-deleting the account via Google. Not exercised by the tests here (no soft-deleted seed), but worth guarding — either exclude soft-deleted from the fallback or reactivate explicitly. Reference: /app/backend/routers/auth.py:116-130.

action_items: Optional: harden /auth/session to skip soft-deleted users on the DuplicateKeyError fallback path (or explicitly clear deleted_at when reactivating via Google).
Optional (carried from prior iterations): swallow the shadow*/pointerEvents RN Web deprecation console warnings — cosmetic only.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/auth.py:88-93 (login) — Password-only guard is correct: `not user OR not user.get('password_hash') OR not _check_pw(...)` short-circuits `_check_pw` on Google-only users (password_hash=None) and the ternary returns 'Esta cuenta usa Google. Entra con Google.' only when the account exists but has no password. Verified indirectly (wrong-password on ana.demo returns the generic 'Email o contraseña incorrectos', not the Google message).

routers/auth.py:100-134 (/auth/session) — Correctly (a) validates via Pydantic (SessionBody with a single required session_id → 422 when missing/renamed), (b) exchanges exactly once server-side against demobackend.emergentagent.com and never leaks the session_id to the client, (c) upserts by lowercased email with unique-index protection via DuplicateKeyError, (d) reuses the same JWT-pair issuer as email/password so every downstream endpoint keeps working unchanged. See minor issue above about soft-deleted resurrection.

auth.tsx:79-93 (frontend) — `exchanged` useRef Set guards against duplicate exchanges of the same session_id from multiple sources (initial URL + deep-link listener). Web behaviour verified: exactly one POST /auth/session per page load with a session_id in the URL, even after a 401. cleanWebUrl() runs only on success (line 91), matching the spec.

auth.tsx:95-106 — On a failed exchange the effect falls through to `reload()`, which restores the stored session (verified: /?session_id=bogus2 while logged in as Ana keeps her on /map via /auth/me 200).
seed_data_creation: None besides one TEST_tester_google_<rand>@sentinelfamily.app registration (idempotent, no group/profile changes). Ana's group is untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Emergent-managed Google sign-in wiring is fully verified end-to-end except for the real Google login (which can't be automated). Backend endpoint POST /api/auth/session is well-formed (401/422 paths correct, Spanish detail), and the frontend /onboarding/account button correctly performs a full-page redirect to auth.emergentagent.com with the origin echoed in the `redirect` query param. Return-path handling is idempotent (one exchange per session_id) and gracefully falls back to the stored session on 401. Only one soft-edge case identified (soft-deleted user resurrection via Google) — not urgent. Regression on /map and /drive with Azure Maps is intact. If further iterations touch /auth/session, prefer to guard against reactivating soft-deleted accounts.
